title: CB Live: Carbon Brief journalists discuss key COP31 outcomes - Carbon Brief
gist: Short announcement of a Carbon Brief CB Live panel on COP31: the summit ran nearly 50 hours late (the longest COP ever), the Turkish-Australian 'Antalya pact' was rejected by the EU, UK and vulnerable nations, and limited progress came on the adaptation fund and action agenda. The piece is mostly a panel/recording notice with little analysis.

insights.claim: COP31 in Antalya, Turkey ended nearly 50 hours after its scheduled close, making it the longest COP in history.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Process breakdown at UN climate talks reduces the weight of multilateral outcomes as policy catalysts.
insights.quote: making it the longest COP in history
insights.locator: COP31 came to a dramatic conclusion

insights.claim: The 'Antalya pact' proposed by the joint Turkish-Australian COP31 presidency was rejected in the summit's final hours by the EU, the UK and several climate-vulnerable nations.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: No overarching COP31 political signal; watch COP32 for any renewed headline commitments.

insights.claim: Limited COP31 progress included agreement on the adaptation fund and a raft of voluntary announcements within the action agenda.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Progress came via voluntary channels rather than negotiated texts.
insights.locator: There was some progress at COP31

insights.claim: Key open questions after COP31 included climate finance, China's role, the just transition mechanism and the potential for COP reform.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: COP reform debate is a live theme following the record-length, failed summit.
